newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - May 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - May 12.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Federal Budget will include an incentive to small business to assist Australian companies in gaining a bigger slice of major projects offered by the private sector and Governments. However, the Government will wait for the results of the Mortimer reviw of industry assistance before implementing major changes to this sector. Page 1.

National Party backbencher Ian Causley has questioned National Party Leader Tim Fischer's future, and will not rule out a challenge to the leadership. Causley would not say who was being nominated as an alternative leader, but Party members are confused about the Nationals' handling of the Wik native title issue. Page 4.

A Federal Government backbench committee has increased its resolve to block further concentration of media ownership, and is openly supporting foreign investment to promote diversity. Coalition backbenchers have expressed concern about the Government's handling of the media issue, especially a lack of formal guidelines on determining new ownership. Page 5.

Political and personal connections are proving to be important as the battle for control of Fairfax newspapers intensifies. Following indications Prime Minister John Howard would be favourable to a break-up of the Fairfax newspapers, various media consortiums are forming to be in good positions in the event of ownership rule changes. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Telecommunications giant Telstra will shed 2500 jobs over the next 12 months after technicians and linesman accepted a A$100 million redundancy package. This is a precursor to Telstra retrenching 22,000 employees over the next three years. Page 1

The Natural Heritage Trust Fund will become a centrepiece of Tuesday's Federal Budget, as the Government concentrates on job creation. The Budget will also contain spending cuts of around A$2 billion, and Prime Minister John Howard says it will contain god news for retired people. Page 1.

Senior sources say the University of Melbourne, Swinburne University and Monash University are all bidding for sites at the A$3 billion Melbourne Docklands development, and the bids will include a proposal for a large private university. The University o Melbourne is the most likely tender to win the private university proposal. Page 1.

Finishing a rowdy three day tour of Tasmania, Independent MP Pauline Hanson said she has the support of National Party elder statesman Sir John Bjelke Petersen and Tasmanian National Party branch vice-president Peter Murray, who is advising her on policy formation. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

A new tax rebate to come into effect on July 1 will cut the income tax savers pay on interest earned on bank accounts and other investments. This will be included in the Federal Budget, as the Government hopes to achieve an improvement in the Budget botto line of A$3 billion, which will cut deeply into spending and health services. Page 1.

Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd managing director James Packer said yesterday he would oppose any compromise proposals that would involve the break-up of PBL takeover target John Fairfax Holdings. His comments come as the Federal Government considers aboishing cross-media ownership rules. Page 1.

Sydney continues to suffer in the wake of storms which caused severe damage to the city over the weekend and deposited 81.4 millimetres of rain. Roofs have been torn off buildings, boats ripped from moorings and 1,500 houses in eastern Sydney were withou power on Sunday night. Page 1.

The NSW Opposition claims about A$67 million of funds for hospitals was not spent last financial year, despite an increased demand for health services. Opposition health spokeswoman Jillian Skinner says work on a breast cancer unit, an upgrading of emergency departments and the construction of new mental health units was not undertaken due to the under-spending. Page 3.
THE AGE

The Federal Budget will include a bonus for older Australians through incentive schemes if they defer pension entitlements for up to five years. The plan would see retirees receiving a maximum bonus of about A$17,700 if they delay taking their pension for a full five years. Page 1.

Tomorrow's Federal Budget is expected to see Federal Health Minister Michael Wooldridge announce an increase in the cost of some optometry services under a move that will see restrictions on the Medicare rebate available to people who visit more than one ptometrist within a specified period. Page 1.

Brett Hume, the Metropolitan Fire Brigade's former technical director, said in a November 1994 report to the brigade's board that he did not recommend the Intergraph computer dispatch system, saying it represented a "very high risk" and was "significantlylacking in its ability to meet MFB requirements". Page 1.

Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett said yesterday the National Gallery of Victoria will close for three years under a two-stage, A$160 million, redevelopment of the building, which will increase exhibition space, add a galleria, and possibly see a floating cafe on the front moat. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
